question: Under Section 2(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended), an 'adapted vehicle' means a motor vehicle specially designed, or adapted, for use by:

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(16) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a goods carriage is classified as a 'heavy goods vehicle' if its gross vehicle weight exceeds:

explanation: Section 2(16) specifies that a tractor or a road-roller is a heavy goods vehicle if the unladen weight of either of which exceeds 12,000 kilograms.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(17) of the MV Act, 1988, a 'heavy passenger motor vehicle' includes any public service vehicle, private service vehicle, educational institution bus or omnibus whose gross vehicle weight or unladen weight exceeds:

explanation: Section 2(21) defines 'light motor vehicle' as a transport vehicle or omnibus the gross vehicle weight of either of which or a motor car or tractor or road-roller the unladen weight of any of which, does not exceed 7,500 kilograms.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: For which type of vehicles does Section 2(21) consider 'unladen weight' rather than 'gross vehicle weight' to determine LMV classification?

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: As defined in Section 2(22) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a 'maxi cab' is a motor vehicle constructed or adapted to carry:

options.A: Not more than 6 passengers excluding the driver

options.C: More than 6 passengers, but not more than 12 passengers, excluding the driver, for hire or reward

question: A goods carriage having a gross vehicle weight of 9,500 kg is classified under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 as a:

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(24) of the MV Act, 1988, a 'medium passenger motor vehicle' has a gross vehicle weight or unladen weight exceeding 7,500 kg but not exceeding:
explanation: Section 2(24) defines 'medium passenger motor vehicle' as having gross vehicle weight or unladen weight exceeding 7,500 kg but not exceeding 12,000 kg.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: According to Section 2(25) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a 'motor cab' is a motor vehicle constructed or adapted to carry:

options.C: Up to 8 passengers including the driver
options.D: Not more than 6 passengers excluding the driver for hire or reward

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: How does the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 define a 'motor car' under Section 2(26)?

options.A: Any motor vehicle having 4 wheels designed for family transport

options.C: Any motor vehicle other than a transport vehicle, omnibus, road-roller, tractor, motor cycle or adapted vehicle
options.D: Any private passenger motor vehicle having engine capacity exceeding 800 cc

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(29) of the MV Act, 1988, an 'omnibus' means any motor vehicle constructed or adapted to carry:

options.A: More than 12 persons excluding the driver
options.B: Up to 6 persons including the driver
options.C: More than 6 persons excluding the driver

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(33) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a 'private service vehicle' is a motor vehicle constructed or adapted to carry more than six persons excluding the driver and used:

options.D: By or on behalf of the owner for carrying persons in connection with his trade or business otherwise than for hire or reward

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which of the following is NOT included within the definition of 'public service vehicle' under Section 2(35) of the MV Act, 1988?

options.A: Stage carriage and contract carriage

explanation: Under Section 2(35), 'public service vehicle' means any motor vehicle used or adapted to be used for the carriage of passengers for hire or reward, and includes a maxi cab, a motor cab, contract carriage, and stage carriage. A private service vehicle is not used for hire/reward.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(47) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a 'transport vehicle' includes which group of vehicles?

options.A: Private motor cars, motorcycles, and invalid carriages

options.C: A public service vehicle, a goods carriage, an educational institution bus or a private service vehicle
options.D: Only stage carriages and national permit goods trucks

explanation: Section 2(47) defines 'transport vehicle' as a public service vehicle, a goods carriage, an educational institution bus or a private service vehicle.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(48) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, what is expressly EXCLUDED when calculating the 'unladen weight' of a motor vehicle?

options.A: Spare tyre and tool kit
options.C: The weight of a driver or attendant

explanation: Section 2(48) states that unladen weight includes all equipment ordinarily used with the vehicle when working, but excludes the weight of a driver or attendant.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a vehicle is equipped with alternative bodies for seasonal operations, how is the 'unladen weight' determined under Section 2(48) of the MV Act, 1988?

options.A: Average weight of all alternative bodies
options.B: Weight of the lightest alternative body
options.D: Weight of the vehicle with the heaviest alternative part or body

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: An educational institution bus is classified as which class of vehicle under Section 2(47) of the MV Act, 1988?

options.A: Special purpose tourist vehicle

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: A tourist tempo traveller registered to carry 11 passengers on hire or reward is legally classified under Section 2(22) as a:

options.A: Motor cab

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a motor vehicle is designed to carry 4 passengers plus driver and operates on hire through digital platform meter fare, it is classified as a:

options.A: Omnibus

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: A multi-axle rigid truck having gross vehicle weight of 28,000 kg falls under which statutory category under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?

options.A: Medium goods vehicle

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which of the following vehicles requires gross vehicle weight not exceeding 7,500 kg to be classified as an LMV?

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under the landmark Supreme Court ruling in Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., a person holding an LMV driving licence is entitled to drive:

options.C: A transport vehicle of LMV class whose gross vehicle weight does not exceed 7,500 kg without separate endorsement
options.D: Only adapted three-wheelers and motor cabs

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the maximum passenger seating capacity permitted in a 'maxi cab' under Section 2(22) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?

options.A: 6 passengers

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(29) of the MV Act, what is the minimum passenger seating capacity that qualifies a vehicle as an 'omnibus'?

options.A: More than 4 persons

question: An articulated vehicle comprises a prime mover and which attached component as per Section 2(2)?

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: In Section 2(15), who is authorized to certify and register the permissible gross vehicle weight of a vehicle?

question: A bus owned by an IT company used exclusively to ferry its employees to the office without charging fares is classified under Section 2(33) as a:

question: A tractor with an unladen weight of 5,500 kg used on roads falls under which statutory category under Section 2(21)?

question: A road-roller having an unladen weight of 14,000 kg is classified under the MV Act, 1988 as a:

question: Under Section 2(1A) of the MV Act, 1988, digital platforms such as Uber and Ola are classified as:

question: Which of the following vehicles is EXCLUDED from the statutory definition of 'motor car' under Section 2(26)?

question: When calculating the gross vehicle weight under the MV Act, what components are included?

question: Which statutory provision of the MV Act defines the term 'transport vehicle'?

question: Which section of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 defines 'gross vehicle weight'?

question: Under Section 2(1A), aggregators must comply with guidelines issued by which authority?

question: A passenger vehicle registered with a seating capacity of 5 passengers excluding driver operating on meter taxi permit is a:

question: What is the lower and upper GVW limit defining a 'medium goods vehicle' under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?

question: Under Section 2(48), unladen weight of a vehicle does NOT include:

question: If an omnibus has a gross vehicle weight of 14,500 kg, it is classified under Section 2(17) as a:

question: Under Section 2(22), what is the minimum seating capacity that separates a maxi cab from a motor cab?

question: Under Section 2(21), what is the unladen weight limit for a tractor to qualify as an LMV?

question: Which term was introduced into Section 2 of the Motor Vehicles Act by the 2019 Amendment to regulate app-based taxi aggregators?

question: Under Section 2(24), an educational institution bus with GVW of 9,000 kg is a:

question: Under Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, driving an unregistered motor vehicle in any public place is:

question: Under the proviso to Section 39, which class of vehicles may be driven without registration under specified conditions?

question: Under Section 52(1) of the MV Act, 1988, what is the fundamental rule regarding alteration of a motor vehicle?

question: Under Section 52 of the MV Act, which alteration is legally permissible with approval/specification by Central Government?

options.D: Removal of brake lights to reduce battery load

question: What did the Supreme Court hold in Regional Transport Officer, Kozhikode v. K.P. Noorudeen regarding structural vehicle modification under Section 52?

options.B: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs
options.D: The Automobile Research Association of India

explanation: Section 213(1) empowers the State Government to establish a Motor Vehicles Department and appoint officers.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: In Kerala, what is the apex administrative post in the Motor Vehicles Department created under Section 213?

options.A: Transport Commissioner

explanation: The Transport Commissioner heads the Motor Vehicles Department in the State.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 213(3), the State Government may authorize officers of the Motor Vehicles Department to exercise powers including:

options.A: Entering and inspecting motor vehicles at all reasonable times
options.B: Stopping and examining vehicles on public roads
options.C: Seizing documents and detaining vehicles under Section 206 and 207

explanation: Section 213(3) authorizes MVD officers to stop, inspect, search, seize documents, and detain vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory entry-level executive/technical inspection cadre in the Kerala Motor Vehicles Department recruited through Kerala PSC?

options.A: Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector (AMVI)

explanation: Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector (AMVI) is the entry-level technical cadre recruited via Kerala PSC.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under the Kerala Motor Vehicles Department hierarchical structure, who is the immediate promotional post for an Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector?

options.A: Motor Vehicles Inspector (MVI)

explanation: An AMVI is promoted to the cadre of Motor Vehicles Inspector (MVI).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 213(4), who prescribes the minimum qualifications for the appointment of Motor Vehicles Inspectors and Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspectors?

options.A: The Central Government

explanation: Section 213(4) provides that the Central Government may prescribe minimum qualifications for MVD inspecting officers.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What are the statutory technical qualifications prescribed by the Central Government for appointment as AMVI/MVI?

options.A: A degree or diploma in Automobile Engineering or Mechanical Engineering from a recognized institution and a valid driving licence authorizing driving of heavy transport vehicles and motorcycles
options.D: High school qualification with no driving licence

explanation: Central Government notification under Section 213(4) prescribes Automobile/Mechanical Engineering degree/diploma and driving licences.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 213(5), what powers does the State Government have regarding uniforms and insignia of MVD officers?

options.A: The State Government may regulate the uniform, insignia, badges, and accoutrements to be worn by officers of the Motor Vehicles Department
options.B: Officers can wear any civilian clothing of their choice
options.C: Uniforms must be identical to the Indian Air Force
options.D: Uniforms can only be worn on national holidays

explanation: Section 213(5) empowers the State Government to regulate uniforms, ranks, and badges of MVD officers.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: In Kerala, what rank insignia is worn on the shoulder epaulettes by an Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector (AMVI)?

options.A: Two Stars with Kerala MVD Ribbon (Navy Blue and Maroon)
options.C: Three Stars with Red and Blue ribbon

explanation: In Kerala MVD uniform regulations, an AMVI wears Two Stars with the departmental ribbon.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What rank insignia is worn by a Motor Vehicles Inspector (MVI) in Kerala?

options.A: Three Stars with Departmental Ribbon

explanation: An MVI in Kerala wears Three Stars with departmental ribbon.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What rank insignia is worn by a Regional Transport Officer (RTO) in Kerala?

options.A: State Emblem of India (Ashoka Emblem) with Departmental Ribbon

explanation: An RTO wears the Ashoka Emblem with departmental ribbon.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can an Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector (AMVI) on enforcement duty stop a private car and check its pollution under control (PUC) certificate and registration?

options.A: Yes, AMVIs are empowered enforcement officers under Section 132, 213, and KMV Rules
options.B: No, AMVIs can only inspect vehicles inside RTO office compounds
options.C: Only if accompanied by the District Collector

explanation: AMVIs possess full enforcement authority under Section 213 and Section 132 to inspect vehicles on public roads.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 213, what functional wing in the Kerala Motor Vehicles Department is specifically dedicated to road safety enforcement, checking over-speeding, and vehicle fitness on highways?

options.A: Safe Kerala Enforcement Squad / Flying Squad

explanation: The Safe Kerala Project and Enforcement Wing (Flying Squads) of MVD handle on-road checking and camera operations.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 213, who acts as the Chairman of the Regional Transport Authority (RTA) in a district in Kerala?

options.A: The District Collector / District Magistrate

explanation: Under KMV Rules, the District Collector is the Chairman of the Regional Transport Authority (RTA).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Who acts as the Secretary of the Regional Transport Authority (RTA) in a district in Kerala?

options.A: The Regional Transport Officer (RTO)

explanation: The Regional Transport Officer (RTO) acts as the Secretary of the RTA.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(e) of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, 'purchase value' means:

options.A: The value of the vehicle as shown in the purchase invoice issued by the manufacturer or dealer, including GST and cess, or determined by the taxation officer where invoice is suspicious or unavailable
options.D: The wholesale price excluding all taxes

explanation: Section 2(e) defines 'purchase value' as the value in the purchase invoice including all taxes and duties, or determined by the taxation officer.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(e), if a vehicle is imported into India, how is the 'purchase value' determined for Kerala road tax?

options.A: The value assessed for customs duty under the Customs Act, 1962, plus all customs duties and levies paid
options.B: The original showroom price in foreign currency converted at 1976 exchange rates

explanation: For imported vehicles, Section 2(e) bases purchase value on the customs assessed value plus all import duties paid.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a vehicle invoice shows large artificial discounts to evade one-time tax, how can the taxation officer determine the purchase value under Section 2(e)?

options.A: The taxation officer may determine purchase value having regard to the price published in the official manufacturer price list for that model
options.B: The officer must accept whatever discount is written
options.C: The officer must forfeit the vehicle to the Governor
options.D: The vehicle cannot be registered in India

explanation: Under the proviso to Section 2(e), the taxation officer can adopt the manufacturer's published price list.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(e), does the 'purchase value' include Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Compensation Cess?

options.A: Yes, purchase value specifically includes all taxes, duties, and cesses charged in the sale invoice
options.D: Only Cess is included, GST is excluded

explanation: The definition under Section 2(e) encompasses the invoice amount including GST and cess.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 2(e), if a vehicle's purchase invoice is missing during transfer from another State, who assesses the purchase value?

options.A: The Taxation Officer having jurisdiction, based on guidelines, depreciation tables, and manufacturer records

explanation: The Taxation Officer is statutorily empowered to determine the purchase value under Section 2(e).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 3(1) of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, tax is levied on:

options.A: Every motor vehicle used or kept for use in the State of Kerala
options.D: Only vehicles operating on national highways

explanation: Section 3(1) levies tax on every motor vehicle 'used or kept for use in the State'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 3(1), when is a vehicle presumed to be 'kept for use in the State'?

options.A: If a certificate of registration or temporary registration has been issued or valid in respect of the vehicle
options.B: Only when the engine is running
options.C: Only when it is parked inside an RTO office

explanation: The explanation to Section 3(1) creates a statutory presumption that a registered vehicle is kept for use in the State.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the system of taxation applicable to non-transport private motor cars and motorcycles in Kerala under Section 3(1)?

options.A: One-time lump sum tax for a period of fifteen (15) years at the time of initial registration
options.D: Toll tax paid at each bridge

explanation: Non-transport private vehicles pay one-time tax for 15 years based on a percentage of purchase value under the Schedule.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: On what basis is One-Time Tax calculated for private motor cars in Kerala?

options.A: As a percentage slab based on the 'Purchase Value' of the motor car
options.B: Based on engine cubic capacity (cc) only
options.D: Based on the number of passenger doors

explanation: In Kerala, one-time tax on private cars is graduated as percentage slabs based on purchase value.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the tax period for commercial stage carriages and goods carriages paying periodic road tax under Section 4 of the Kerala MV Taxation Act?

options.A: Quarterly (tax paid for three months in advance)

explanation: Commercial transport vehicles generally pay tax quarterly under the Kerala MV Taxation Act.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: On what basis is motor vehicle tax levied on a Stage Carriage in Kerala under the Schedule to Section 3?

options.A: Per passenger seat (and per standing passenger) permitted to be carried per quarter

explanation: Stage carriages are taxed based on seating and standing capacity per quarter.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: On what basis is periodic motor vehicle tax levied on a Goods Carriage in Kerala under Section 3?

options.A: Based on Registered Gross Vehicle Weight (Registered Laden Weight - RLW)

explanation: Goods carriage tax is graduated based on Gross Vehicle Weight / Registered Laden Weight.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 3, who is the 'Taxation Officer' appointed to collect tax under the Act?

options.A: The Regional Transport Officer (RTO) or Joint Regional Transport Officer (Joint RTO) or other designated officer

explanation: RTOs and Joint RTOs function as Taxation Officers under the Kerala MV Taxation Act.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Section 3A of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976 provides for the levy of:

options.A: Green Tax

explanation: Section 3A specifically provides for the levy of 'Green Tax'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 3A, Green Tax is levied on transport vehicles having completed what age?

options.A: More than 10 years (or 7 years for specified commercial categories) from date of registration

explanation: Under Section 3A and Schedule, Green Tax applies to transport vehicles completing designated age (e.g. 10/15 years).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 3A, Green Tax is levied on non-transport vehicles (private cars) completing what age at the time of renewal of registration?

options.A: 15 years from registration, levied for a period of 5 years

explanation: For non-transport private vehicles, Green Tax is levied at the time of 15-year registration renewal for a 5-year block.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory objective of levying Green Tax under Section 3A?

options.A: To discourage the continued use of older, polluting vehicles and generate funds to tackle environmental pollution
options.D: To replace all trees along highways

explanation: Green Tax disincentivizes older polluting vehicles and finances environmental/road safety initiatives.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Are fully electric vehicles (EVs) liable to pay Green Tax under Section 3A?

options.A: No, zero-emission electric vehicles are exempt from Green Tax
options.B: Yes, EVs pay double Green Tax
options.C: Only electric buses pay Green Tax

explanation: Zero-emission electric vehicles do not emit tailpipe pollutants and are exempt from Green Tax.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the validity period of Green Tax paid for an older transport vehicle under Section 3A in Kerala?

options.A: One year (paid annually at the time of fitness certificate renewal)

explanation: For transport vehicles, Green Tax is paid annually alongside the annual fitness renewal.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 3A, is Green Tax payable in addition to the normal road tax payable under Section 3?

options.A: Yes, Green Tax is levied in addition to any tax levied under Section 3
options.B: No, Green Tax replaces normal tax
options.C: Only 10% of Green Tax is payable
options.D: Green Tax is deducted from normal tax

explanation: Section 3A explicitly specifies that Green Tax is levied 'in addition to the tax leviable under Section 3'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4(1) of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, tax must be paid:

options.A: In advance, within the prescribed grace period from the commencement of the tax period
options.B: At the end of the year
options.C: Only when the vehicle is sold
options.D: Only when the vehicle is involved in an accident

explanation: Section 4(1) requires tax to be paid in advance within the prescribed period (grace period).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the standard grace period allowed under the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Rules for payment of quarterly tax without penalty?

options.A: 14 days (or up to 45 days as notified by Government for specific quarters)

explanation: The standard statutory grace period is 14 days from commencement of quarter, frequently extended up to 30 or 45 days by notification.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4(2), upon payment of tax, what document is granted to the owner?

options.A: A tax licence (or digital tax receipt / tax token) in the prescribed form

explanation: Section 4(2) provides that the Taxation Officer shall issue a tax licence in the prescribed form.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4, what happens to the tax licence when a motor vehicle is used in a public place?

options.A: The tax licence or receipt must be carried in the vehicle or verifiable electronically through Vahan
options.B: It must be deposited in the district court
options.C: It must be framed at home
options.D: It must be mailed to the Governor

explanation: Tax payment proof must be available for inspection in physical or digital form (Vahan/mParivahan).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4, can road tax in Kerala be paid online?

options.A: Yes, through the Parivahan / e-Payment portal of the Motor Vehicles Department
options.B: No, tax can only be paid in gold coins at the Secretariat
options.C: Only cash payments at local post offices are permitted
options.D: Only cheques drawn on foreign banks are accepted

explanation: Modern tax collection is fully automated online via the national Parivahan portal.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4(1), who is primarily responsible for the payment of tax?

options.A: The registered owner or the person having possession or control of the motor vehicle

explanation: The registered owner or person having possession/control is statutorily liable to pay the tax.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 5(1) of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, what is the procedure to obtain tax exemption when a vehicle is NOT in use?

options.A: The owner must file a prior intimation of non-use in Form G to the Taxation Officer before the commencement of the quarter/period
options.B: The owner can simply stop paying tax without telling anyone
options.C: The owner can send a WhatsApp text after 6 months
options.D: The owner can dismantle the engine without notice

explanation: Section 5(1) requires prior filing of non-use application in Form G before commencement of the period.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory form used for intimation of non-use under Rule 10 of Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Rules?

options.A: Form G

explanation: Form G is the prescribed statutory form for claiming tax exemption due to non-use.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 5, what must the owner specify in Form G regarding the non-use of the vehicle?

options.A: The exact place where the vehicle is garaged, the period of non-use, and the reasons for non-use
options.D: The cost of next year's tyres

explanation: Form G requires specifying the garaging location, period of non-use, and reasons (e.g. major mechanical repair).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can an Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector inspect the garaged vehicle to verify the genuineness of Form G non-use?

options.A: Yes, physical verification of the vehicle at the declared garage is a routine duty of inspecting officers (AMVI/MVI)
options.B: No, officers are legally prohibited from inspecting garaged vehicles
options.C: Only if the vehicle caught fire
options.D: Only with a search warrant from the High Court

explanation: AMVIs conduct physical inspection of the garage to ensure the vehicle is genuinely not in use.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a vehicle for which Form G non-use exemption was claimed is caught plying on a public road during the exemption period:

options.A: The exemption is revoked, and full tax along with maximum penalty and legal prosecution is initiated
options.C: The vehicle is declared an ambulance
options.D: No action can be taken because Form G was filed

explanation: Plying during Form G non-use constitutes tax fraud, attracting full tax, heavy penalties under Section 12, and detention.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the maximum period of non-use exemption that can be granted on a single Form G application?

options.A: Up to six months (or one year as prescribed under rules, subject to extension on fresh application)

explanation: Non-use is granted for specified quarters (normally up to 6 months/1 year) and requires fresh application for further periods.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 5(2), who is empowered to grant exemption from payment of tax to any class of vehicles in public interest?

options.A: The State Government, by notification in the Gazette

explanation: Section 5(2) empowers the State Government to exempt any vehicle or class of vehicles from tax by notification.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which vehicles are granted statutory or notified exemption from road tax under Section 5 in Kerala?

options.A: Agricultural tractors and power tillers used solely for agricultural purposes, and adapted vehicles of disabled persons

explanation: Agricultural tractors used solely for farming and adapted vehicles used by disabled persons are exempt.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 6 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, when is an owner entitled to a refund of road tax?

options.A: When tax has been paid in advance and the vehicle has not been used on public roads for a continuous period of not less than one whole calendar month
options.C: If the vehicle travels less than 1,000 km in a year
options.D: If the owner moves to another house in the same town

explanation: Section 6 provides for refund where tax was paid in advance and the vehicle was not used for one or more full calendar months.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 6, what is the minimum continuous period of non-use required to claim a refund of tax?

options.A: One whole calendar month

explanation: Section 6 explicitly specifies non-use for 'a continuous period of not less than one whole calendar month'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What MUST the owner surrender to the Taxation Officer to claim a tax refund under Section 6?

options.A: The tax licence / token and certificate of registration, along with proof of non-use
options.C: The vehicle keys to the driver

explanation: Under Section 6 and Rule 14, the tax licence and RC must be surrendered to establish continuous non-use.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a partial refund of one-time tax (15-year tax) be claimed if a private car is permanently removed from Kerala to another State?

options.A: Yes, pro-rata refund for the unexpired balance of the 15-year period is admissible under Section 6 and the Schedule
options.B: No, one-time tax is completely non-refundable under all circumstances
options.C: Only if the new state has zero road tax

explanation: When a vehicle is permanently removed on change of address to another state, pro-rata refund for unexpired quarters is admissible.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 6, within what time from the expiry of the period must an application for refund be submitted?

options.A: Within the prescribed time limit (normally within 3 months / 6 months of expiry of period)

explanation: Refund applications must be filed within the prescribed statutory limitation period under KMV Taxation Rules.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 7 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, when does liability to pay 'Additional Tax' arise?

options.A: When a motor vehicle is altered or used in a manner that causes it to become liable to tax at a higher rate than what was paid
options.B: When the vehicle is washed with shampoo
options.D: When the car travels into another district

explanation: Section 7 mandates additional tax when vehicle alterations or usage changes push it into a higher tax bracket.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If an educational institution bus paying concessional tax is used on weekends as a commercial contract carriage carrying tourists:

options.A: Additional tax under Section 7 is payable at the contract carriage rate for the relevant period

explanation: Changing use to a higher-rated commercial contract carriage triggers additional tax liability under Section 7.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a truck's seating capacity or registered laden weight is increased by structural alteration, the owner must pay additional tax under:

options.A: Section 7

explanation: Increasing GVW increases the tax slab, requiring additional tax under Section 7.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 7, how is the additional tax calculated?

options.A: The difference between the tax payable at the higher rate and the tax already paid for the unexpired portion of the period
options.B: Double the entire purchase value of the vehicle
options.D: Triple the annual budget of the RTO

explanation: Section 7 specifies payment of an additional tax of a sum equal to the difference between higher tax and tax already paid.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 10 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, who is empowered to stop a motor vehicle in any public place?

options.A: Any Officer of the Police or Motor Vehicles Department not below the prescribed rank

explanation: Section 10 empowers officers of Police or Motor Vehicles Department not below prescribed rank (AMVI and above) to stop vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the purpose of stopping a vehicle under Section 10?

options.A: To inspect the tax licence or satisfy themselves that tax has been paid in respect of the vehicle
options.C: To borrow petrol from the tank

explanation: The statutory purpose under Section 10 is checking tax licences and verifying payment of tax under the Act.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 10, what is the duty of the driver when signaled to stop by an AMVI in uniform?

options.A: The driver shall immediately stop the vehicle and keep it stationary until the officer permits him to proceed
options.B: The driver should accelerate and escape
options.C: The driver should switch off lights and honk
options.D: The driver has no obligation to stop

explanation: Section 10 mandates that the driver shall stop and remain stationary until permitted to proceed.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 11 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, an authorized officer may seize and detain a motor vehicle if:

options.A: The tax due in respect of the vehicle has not been paid within the prescribed time
options.B: The vehicle is older than 3 years
options.C: The driver does not carry an ATM card

explanation: Section 11 empowers authorized officers to seize and detain vehicles in respect of which tax has not been paid.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 11, for how long can a vehicle seized for tax default be detained in custody?

options.A: Until the tax due, together with penalty and custody charges, is fully paid

explanation: The vehicle remains detained under Section 11 until all tax arrears, penalties, and custody expenses are satisfied.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 11, if the tax and penalty remain unpaid after due notice, what power does the Taxation Officer have?

options.A: Power to sell the motor vehicle by public auction to recover the tax arrears and expenses
options.B: Power to give the vehicle to his relatives
options.C: Power to push the vehicle into the sea
options.D: Power to dismantle the vehicle for scrap without public auction

explanation: Section 11 authorizes selling the detained motor vehicle in public auction to recover outstanding dues.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can an Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector in Kerala seize a commercial bus for default of quarterly road tax under Section 11?

options.A: Yes, AMVIs are authorized officers under notifications issued under Section 11
options.B: No, only the District Judge can seize vehicles
options.C: Only if the bus is registered in another country
options.D: Only if the bus has no passengers

explanation: AMVIs and MVIs are designated authorized officers under Section 11 to seize and detain tax-defaulting vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 12 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, what is payable when tax is not paid within the prescribed due date?

options.A: Additional tax by way of penalty (penal interest/penalty at prescribed percentage slabs)

explanation: Section 12 prescribes additional tax by way of penalty for default in payment of tax within the due date.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Rules, what is the maximum penalty percentage leviable under Section 12 for prolonged tax default?

options.A: Up to 50% (or 100% of the tax due depending on the duration of default exceeding six months)

explanation: Penalties under Section 12 are graduated based on duration of default, reaching up to 50% or 100% of the tax due.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 12, can the Taxation Officer waive the penalty if sufficient cause is shown for non-payment?

options.A: Yes, if the officer is satisfied that the failure was due to circumstances beyond control and not willful neglect
options.B: No, the officer has zero discretion under any circumstances
options.C: Only if the owner pays a private fee

explanation: Under prescribed rules and Section 12, penalty may be mitigated/waived on proof of genuine unavoidable circumstances.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 13 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, any amount due on account of tax, penalty, or interest may be recovered:

options.A: As arrears of land revenue under the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968
options.C: By deducting salary of the AMVI
options.D: By seizing the vehicle driver's school certificates

explanation: Section 13 explicitly provides that tax, penalty, and interest are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What powers are available under the Revenue Recovery (RR) Act when tax arrears are recovered under Section 13?

options.A: Attachment and sale of movable and immovable properties of the defaulting owner, and arrest/detention in civil jail in case of fraudulent evasion
options.B: Publishing photos on highway banners only

explanation: Revenue recovery proceedings under Section 13 enable attachment and sale of immovable land/buildings and movable assets.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Does the recovery of tax under Section 13 bar the department from also seizing the vehicle under Section 11?

options.A: No, remedies under Section 11 (seizure of vehicle) and Section 13 (revenue recovery) are concurrent and cumulative until tax is satisfied
options.B: Yes, only one remedy can be chosen
options.C: Seizure of vehicle is illegal once RR notice is issued
options.D: RR proceedings can only be initiated after vehicle is auctioned

explanation: The departmental remedies of vehicle detention and revenue recovery operate concurrently to secure public revenue.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 26 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, 'escaped assessment' empowers the Taxation Officer to:

options.A: Assess or re-assess tax that has escaped assessment or has been under-assessed within the prescribed limitation period
options.C: Double the tax arbitrarily without notice

explanation: Section 26 gives power to assess or re-assess tax which has escaped assessment or was assessed at too low a rate.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 26, before making an assessment of escaped tax, what MUST the Taxation Officer serve on the owner?

options.A: A notice giving the owner a reasonable opportunity of being heard (show-cause notice)
options.C: A demand for cash deposit within 1 hour
options.D: A demolition notice for the vehicle

explanation: Section 26 requires issuing a notice to the owner and affording a reasonable opportunity of showing cause.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory limitation period for reopening an escaped assessment under Section 26?

options.A: Within four (4) years from the end of the year to which the tax relates

explanation: Section 26 specifies a limitation period of four years from the end of the relevant tax year.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If an owner registers a luxury car in Puducherry using fake address documents to evade high Kerala road tax, can Kerala MVD assess escaped tax under Section 26?

options.A: Yes, if the vehicle is kept or used in Kerala, tax can be assessed under Section 3 read with Section 26 along with penalties
options.B: No, Puducherry registration grants absolute permanent immunity in Kerala
options.C: Only if the owner is arrested by Puducherry police
options.D: Kerala has no jurisdiction over vehicles with PY registration

explanation: Under Section 3 and Section 26, vehicles kept or used in Kerala are subject to Kerala tax regardless of fraudulent outside registration.
